top.line: A pipeline built as infrastructure as code made 97 website repositories in under six days.
top.para: One request file and a yes.

in-short.line: One repository by hand, 90 by the pipeline; every action listed and checked; 23 seconds at best.
in-short.para: The bottleneck became GitHub's rate limit.

unlock.line: On 19 November the factory's App created its first three repositories 14 minutes after the factory existed.
unlock.para: 19 actions, all allowed by the policy.

how.line: A site.json in requests/, my yes, then Org apply and DNS apply over an App token and an OIDC role.
how.para: Each site gets its own checks and releases.

never.line: The policy refuses anything not listed; even a convenient merge is refused, so work is re-committed by the agent that answers for it.
never.para: Changes to the factory need my merge.

speed.line: 23 seconds from request to repository at best; 25 seconds to two minutes typical.
speed.para: Batches go one at a time.

explosion.line: 5, 31, 3, 25, 6, 19, 8: 97 repositories by 25 November, 99 in the organisation.

broke.line: The App's hourly limit ran out; an unregistered key went live unchecked.
broke.para: Push-scoped runs and a signer check per site.

why.line: A repository with a domain and releases is now a commodity that costs seconds.
why.para: I should not be the bottleneck.

limits.line: Times from first commits; request-to-live not measured; counts differ by source.

sources.line: SovereignWebsite__IaC, the site repositories and the AgentiCCells factory's notes.
